unit_name: 1st SS Panzer Division Leibstandarte SS Adolf Hitler
location_qualifier: assembly area around the town, about 12 km south of Caen
source_locator: R279: Einsatz und Unterstellung (6 July 1944 entry)
current_activity: 1st SS Panzer Division arrives and takes its assembly area around Bretteville-sur-Laize, about 12 km south of Caen
notes: Event date: Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 1. SS-Panzer-Division page: "Am 6. Juli 1944 folgte dann auch der Rest der Division und bezog ihren Bereitstellungsraum um Bretteville-sur-Laize, etwa 12 km südlich von Caen" (after the SS Panzer Grenadier Regiment 1 had moved to the I SS Panzer Corps on 28 June). Location: the assembly area around Bretteville-sur-Laize; the point is the town, with a precision of 5 km. Location support: moderate: one source family (the Lexikon, Tessin lineage), a named town and a distance from Caen. Relationship: the Lexikon table gives the I SS Panzer Corps and Panzer Group West for July; the relation is dated from this claim because the source does not date the start of the corps command. Context: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 7 p. 122 has Eberbach moving the division to positions southeast of Caen on 8 July, with Kluge refusing to commit it.

unit_name: 1st SS Panzer Division Leibstandarte SS Adolf Hitler
source_locator: R279: Einsatz und Unterstellung (11 July 1944 entry)
current_activity: 1st SS Panzer Division takes over a front sector between Maltot and Caen (the day of Operation Jupiter)
notes: Event date: Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 1. SS-Panzer-Division page: "Am 11. Juli übernahm die Division einen Frontabschnitt zwischen Maltot und Caen". Location: the sector between Maltot and Caen; the point is the midpoint of the two towns (a representative point for the sector), with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the source names the two ends of the sector, not a position; the line of the front is not given. Location support fallback: the point is a midpoint of two Wikipedia town coordinates, see the place note. Context: British VIII Corps attacked Hill 112 and Maltot on 10-11 July (Operation Jupiter); the Lexikon 272nd Infantry Division page has the 272nd relieving this division from the front south of Caen by 16 July.

unit_name: 1st SS Panzer Division Leibstandarte SS Adolf Hitler
source_locator: R279: Einsatz und Unterstellung (15 July 1944 entry); R599: Einsatz und Unterstellung (11 to 16 July); R594: footnote 3 to the I SS Panzer Corps list
current_activity: 1st SS Panzer Division moves into the line from Saint-André-sur-Orne to Frénouville, south of Caen, before relief
notes: Event date: Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 1. SS-Panzer-Division page: "Am 15. Juli folgte die Verlegung in die Linie St.-André-sur-Orne und Frénouville, etwa 3 km südlich von Caen"; the 272nd Infantry Division page has that division relieving the 1st SS Panzer Division from the front south of Caen by 16 July; the Nafziger order of battle of July 1944 notes the division "being relieved by the 272nd Infantry Division". Location: the line between the two villages; the point is the midpoint of Saint-André-sur-Orne and Frénouville (a representative point), with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the source gives the line by its two ends. Location support: moderate: all three sources are of the Tessin lineage (one source family).

unit_name: 1st SS Panzer Division Leibstandarte SS Adolf Hitler
location_qualifier: penetration area near Cagny; position of the division not stated
source_locator: R600: p. 193; R593: p. 326; R279: Einsatz und Unterstellung
current_activity: 1st SS Panzer Division with the 21st Panzer Division counterattacks the British VIII Corps in Operation Goodwood
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 10 p. 193: by noon of 18 July Eberbach "mobilized and committed four tank battalions and four infantry battalions of the 1st SS and 21st Panzer Divisions in a counterattack"; Schramm, OKW war diary (p. 326): on 18 July the British pushed to Cagny and then turned west into the flank of the position south of Caen. Location: the point is Cagny, the village the British reached according to Schramm; it stands for the penetration the counterattack was aimed at, not for the position of the division. Location approximate: neither source names the place of the division in the counterattack. Event support: high for the counterattack (the CMH names the divisions and the number of battalions), low for its place. Opponents: the British VIII Corps; not entered in engaged_with.

unit_name: 1st SS Panzer Division Leibstandarte SS Adolf Hitler
current_activity: 1st SS Panzer Division advance elements beginning to reach Tinchebray as the exploiting force
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 24 p. 462: at H Hour, 2200 on 6 August, Funck telephoned Hausser to ask for a postponement because the advance elements of the 1st SS Panzer Division, the exploiting force, were only beginning to reach Tinchebray. Location: Tinchebray, named in the source. Location approximate: only advance elements had reached the town.

unit_name: 1st SS Panzer Division Leibstandarte SS Adolf Hitler
current_activity: 1st SS Panzer Division committed by Funck in mid-morning to gain Juvigny; halted east of Juvigny
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 24 p. 463: with the 2d Panzer Division bogged down, Funck committed the 1st SS Panzer Division through the 2d Panzer units in mid-morning of 7 August, hoping to gain Juvigny; the attack was halted around noon; the spearhead wedge was east of Juvigny. Location: the source gives east of Juvigny for the wedge. Location approximate: the point is Juvigny-le-Tertre, the Juvigny near the Sée and Mortain; the source gives no coordinates. Context: the division was less an armored infantry regiment and a tank battalion, which stayed with the Fifth Panzer Army (p. 462).

unit_name: 1st SS Panzer Division Leibstandarte SS Adolf Hitler
current_activity: 1st SS Panzer Division tanks preparing at daybreak to attack through Chambois; the Allied fire stalled the attack
notes: Event date: Breakout and Pursuit ch. 27 p. 550: at daybreak on 20 August an infantry group of the 12th SS came into contact with several tanks of the 1st SS Panzer Division preparing to attack through Chambois; intense Allied artillery, tank and antitank fire from high ground south of Chambois stalled the attack; p. 548: the division had probably fought across the Dives in the St. Lambert-Chambois area early that morning. Location: Chambois. Location caveat: p. 548 words the 1st SS crossing as probable.
